newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges dip, Russia straight-run pressured.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges dip, Russia straight-run pressured.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges started the week a shade softer with little bunker demand while traders said Russian straight-run continued to be pressured by improving refining margins and strong Russian exports.
High sulphur barges traded once at $94.50 fob Rotterdam early in the day, compared with Friday's highest deal at $95. Later offers were at $95/$95.50 while bids stood at $94.
"It's a typically slow Monday morning. There's hardly any bunker demand," one trader said.
Others said they were disappointed by a the slow start to the week, adding they had expected many more enquiries after Friday's trade was dulled by Assumption Day holiday.
"There were a few enquiries, some bid ones, but they were exptremely low numbers, at $93," another trader said.

On the cargo front, the picture was almost unchanged from the end of last week, with Russian cracked and straight-run roughly assessed at about the same levels. The latter was put at about $93.50/$94 cif a tonne and the former some $1 lower.
"These days there's a very fine line between cracked and straight-run," one trader said. "There's several cargoes of straight-run out there looking for homes."
